turns.doctor_question: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?
turns.patient_response:
Well, I came in 'cause my family and friends, they keep waving these bank papers in my face, saying it proves nothing was taken. But I ain't stupid. For over a year now I’ve known they’re hiding my money. They show me these papers, and the ink on 'em is always smudged. Reminds me of when I used to try and write with those cheap pens from the dollar store. The one over on 5th Street, you know? They closed it down a while back. It's a real shame 'cause they had good peppermint candy. 

But yeah, they're using all this stuff to cover it up—fake bills, these fundraisers they keep bringing up, even trip plans. My aunt keeps talking about planning a trip to Ohio. Who even goes to Ohio for fun? It's just corn and flat roads everywhere. I rode through there once and the radio only played country music for like four hours straight. 

But I know it's all just a trick to hide what they did with my money, so I just have to keep confronting them about it. I'm gonna keep at it until they finally tell the truth. Did you see the magazines out in the waiting room, by the way? They're all from like three years ago.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient expresses a fixed, false belief that their family and friends are hiding their money and using elaborate tricks to cover it up, despite being shown bank papers proving otherwise.
symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient's speech exhibits tangentiality and derailment, frequently wandering off-topic to discuss cheap pens, a closed dollar store, peppermint candy, Ohio's landscape, country music, and waiting room magazines.

Voices? No, no, I don't hear any voices. Just my own thoughts, you know? And the TV, of course. I leave the TV on a lot, mostly for background noise. I was watching this documentary the other day about deep-sea fishing. Did you know they can catch crabs that are like, three feet wide? It's terrifying. I could never go out on the ocean like that. The water is just so dark and you have no idea what's underneath you. My uncle used to have a boat, a little aluminum thing he took out on the lake. We went out once and the motor died right in the middle. We had to paddle back with these tiny plastic oars. Took us like three hours, and I got the worst sunburn on my shoulders. 

But anyway, no, no voices. Just my family lying to my face about my bank accounts.

Other than the arguments with them about the money, I still handle my own meals, get myself down to the county clinic, and make it to my assistance appointments. I keep my things in order the exact same way I always have. I'm very organized, actually. I keep all my important papers in this little blue folder. It's got little daisies printed on it. I found it at a yard sale a few years ago. The lady running it was selling all these old records, too. Tons of them, like, big stacks of vinyl. I don't even have a record player, but I almost bought one just because the covers looked so neat. They had that old, dusty smell, you know? Like an antique shop. I love antique shops, but they always charge too much for old glass bottles. I don't know why people collect those anyway. 

But yeah, I still take care of my day-to-day stuff just fine. They just want you to think I can't so they can keep stealing from me.

turns.doctor_question: Has anyone ever given you a convincing explanation that your money is actually where it should be?
turns.patient_response:
Convincing? No, never. I mean, my family and friends, they keep waving these bank papers in my face, saying it proves nothing was taken. Bank papers. You know, the ones they print on that really thin, cheap paper? It always gives me paper cuts. I got a terrible paper cut just last week opening a letter. It bled right onto the envelope, and I had to use one of those little round bandaids. The ones that never actually stick to your finger right? My cousin bought a whole box of them for her kid's school fundraiser. 

Which, by the way, speaking of fundraisers, that's exactly what they do! They use these fake fundraisers, and bills, and all these big plans for trips to cover up where my money is actually going. For over a year now, I’ve known they’re hiding it. Like my cousin talking about a trip to Florida. Florida! It's so humid there. I went to Florida when I was little and my hair just frizzed up like a poodle. I don't even like the beach anyway, the sand gets everywhere. You find it in your shoes for months, it's disgusting. 

But anyway, no, I don't believe their little papers. I just have to keep confronting them until they finally tell the truth.

symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient's speech demonstrates significant tangentiality and derailment, wandering from the topic of bank papers to paper cuts, bandaids, and Florida beach sand before returning to the original point.

She used to make the best strawberry jam. We'd go picking in the summer, and my hands would be stained red for days. It was so hot out there in the fields, but she always wore this big straw hat with a green ribbon.

turns.doctor_question: When you’re talking with other people, do they ever tell you that your speech is hard to follow or doesn’t make sense?

She just looked at me like I was speaking a different language. I hate those self-checkout machines, too. They always yell at you about an unexpected item in the bagging area. It's like, I just put my bread down, calm down! Bread is so expensive now, too. I used to get that nice sourdough from the bakery down the street, but they closed last month. The owner retired and moved to Florida. Florida seems too hot to me. All that humidity, it makes your hair frizz up. My sister went to Florida once for a vacation and she said she got sunburned on the very first day. She had to sit in the hotel room with aloe vera all over her back. Aloe vera is a funny plant, isn't it? It looks like a cactus but it's squishy inside. I tried to grow one on my windowsill, but I think I watered it too much and it turned brown and died. I'm not very good with plants. 

But no, nobody tells me I'm hard to follow. I think I explain things pretty clearly.

turns.doctor_question: Do you think anything unusual or impossible is happening to your money, or is it more that someone you know is secretly taking it?
turns.patient_response:
It’s not impossible, it’s just... it’s them. My family, my friends, they’re the ones doing it. I came in here because they keep shoving these bank papers in my face, telling me it proves nothing is missing, but I know. For over a year, I’ve known they’re hiding my money. They try to cover it up with all these excuses—like, oh, this bill had to be paid, or we need to donate to this fundraiser, or we’re planning a trip. A trip! Who plans a trip right now? She bought this really ugly tourist t-shirt from the hotel gift shop just to have something clean. Gift shops are such a rip-off, anyway. They charge you five dollars for a tiny bottle of water. I started carrying my own water bottle everywhere, one of those metal ones that keeps the ice cold all day. But you have to wash the straw part really well or it gets moldy. I use a little tiny brush for it, the kind they make for baby bottles. Babies are so much work. I don't know how people do it, waking up every two hours. 

But yeah, they use all these fake expenses to hide what they’re taking, and I just have to keep confronting them until they finally admit the truth. They think I don't see it, but I do.
